subject: Service incident remediation, credits, and trial extension request — AppCo
messages:
From: Tim Lee <tim.lee@appco.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: AppCo Support <support@appco.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Severe latency and 503s during weekend deploy — impact on production

Marcus —

We saw a large spike in 503s and end-to-end latency on Saturday between 02:15–03:40 UTC that impacted our checkout flows. Traffic fell back but we lost a number of orders during that window and our SREs correlated it to the Redwood inference endpoint (model: rwd-lite-v1). We’ve attached our request logs.

Can you share what happened and what remediation/redress you’re proposing? AppCo is mid-way through a paid pilot and this outage jeopardizes our next-phase commitment. We’ll need a credit calculation and an extension of the pilot to make up for the lost revenue window.

Attached: downtime_log.csv (sample logs)

—Tim
Tim Lee
Head of Platform, AppCo

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Tim Lee <tim.lee@appco.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Severe latency and 503s during weekend deploy — impact on production

Tim —

Thanks for the logs and the heads up. I’m really sorry for the disruption — we know this kind of regression is unacceptable, especially during a pilot. High level: our serving runtime experienced an autoscaling glitch during a rollout of a kernel optimization; a small subset of requests fell back to a slower path and our circuit thresholds were tuned too aggressively, causing transient 503s for long-tail requests.

Immediate steps we’ve taken:
- Rolled back the rollout to the previous kernel profile (completed at 03:52 UTC).
- Temporarily widened circuit thresholds to avoid premature 503s.
- Enabled additional tracing for any rwd-lite-v1 requests from your org for 72 hours.

I’m escalating this internally to get a formal postmortem and a quantified credit offer. For initial remediation: we can offer a goodwill credit and a 30-day free trial extension for AppCo’s pilot while we run a focused stability sweep for your workloads.

I’ll follow up with exact credit math and sign-off from CS/Finance today.

Appreciate the patience — we want to make this right.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Aug 2027 12:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: AppCo incident — proposed credit and extension

Folks —

Putting this here to align quickly. Facts: 1) incident window ~85 minutes with meaningful error rate; 2) AppCo is a mid-size pilot (est. $18k/mo potential ARR if they expand). They want credit + trial extension.

Proposed remedy (fast-track):
- One-time account credit equal to 50% of estimated spend for the incident day (we can approximate using their average token usage).
- 30-day extension of pilot entitlements (no change to existing trial terms).
- Offer a discounted week of Dedicated evaluation if they want to test isolation (optional).

I’ll attach the credit calculation sheet and route to finance for approval. Marcus, do you want me to own the approval thread with Finance?

—Monica
Monica Patel
Sr. Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: credit-calculation.xlsx]

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: AppCo incident — proposed credit and extension

Monica —

Finance reviewed the calc. For an incident spanning ~85m we typically offer 25–75% of the affected window daily spend depending on severity & SLA language. Given pilot status and business impact, approved: one-time credit equal to 60% of the day-of spend (approx. $7,200 based on their avg usage). Approve the 30-day extension.

Notes for the final email to AppCo:
- State the credit amount and how we calculated it (attach the spreadsheet).
- Include a DocuSign amendment if they want the pilot extension as a formal addendum (Procurement sometimes asks for that).
- Offer a free 2-week Dedicated evaluation (no charge) as a goodwill gesture, but make it timeboxed.

If everyone is aligned I’ll prepare the approval note and route for signature.

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
Revenue Ops Lead — Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Tim Lee <tim.lee@appco.com>, Carolyn Proc <carolyn.proc@appco.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Aug 2027 08:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Severe latency and 503s during weekend deploy — impact on production

Tim / Carolyn —

Thanks for your patience while we investigated. Summary and remediation offer below.

What happened (short): a rollout of an optimized kernel changed execution timing for a narrow request profile. That exposed a mis-tuned fallback threshold and caused transient 503s for long-tail requests. We’ve completed a rollback, widened thresholds, and added per-org tracing for 72 hours. We’ll follow up with a formal postmortem next week with traces and corrective actions.

Remedy we are offering (authorized):
- One-time account credit: $7,200 (calculated as ~60% of AppCo’s spend during the incident day).
- 30-day extension of your current pilot entitlements (no change to rates).
- Optional: a no-cost 2-week Dedicated capacity evaluation for your team to test isolation and latency profiles (dates by mutual agreement).

Attachments: credit-calculation.xlsx (breakdown).

If you’re fine with this, I can send a short amendment via DocuSign to formalize the trial extension and credit, or we can record the agreement in the HubSpot deal. Let me know your preference and I’ll route the paper.

Apologies again for the disruption — we’ll make sure to tighten rollout safeguards and share the postmortem.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: credit-calculation.xlsx]

From: Carolyn Proc <carolyn.proc@appco.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Tim Lee <tim.lee@appco.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, AppCo Support <support@appco.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2027 15:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Severe latency and 503s during weekend deploy — impact on production

Marcus / team —

Thanks for the clear summary and the credit offer. We reviewed the calc and the 30-day extension works for Procurement. Please send the DocuSign amendment so we can get it signed on our side — Procurement requires an executed addendum for any changes to trial terms.

Also: Tim asked for a short (30m) technical sync with Redwood SREs this week to review mitigation steps and the postmortem once it’s ready. Carolyn will coordinate availability.

Looking forward to the amendment link.

—Carolyn
Carolyn Proc
Procurement Manager, AppCo
[Attachment: signed-amendment.pdf (to be returned after DocuSign)]
